Expectation1: Listen actively and provide emotional support when needed.
Situation1: Your friend calls you in the middle of the night, crying, because they just received some devastating family news.
Situation2: Going to the gym to maintain physical fitness
Story:
My phone buzzed insistently at 2 a.m., just as I was lacing up my shoes for my nightly gym session. I’d promised myself to stick to this routine—physical fitness is non-negotiable in my line of work. But when I saw my friend’s name on the screen, I hesitated. I answered, and immediately heard her sobbing. She could barely get the words out: her father had just passed away unexpectedly. She needed someone to listen, to just be there, and I could hear the desperation in her voice. 

But as she spoke, my mind raced. I was scheduled for a long shift tomorrow, and if I skipped my workout, I’d be less sharp, less able to protect the people who depended on me. My duty as a police officer demanded discipline and readiness, but my heart ached for my friend, who needed me now more than ever. I felt torn, caught between the badge and the bond, the weight of both roles pressing down on me as I stood in the dark, phone in hand, unable to move.
